record.original_question: Determine the border subrank of a generic tensor, and characterize conditions under which a tensor has border subrank strictly higher than the generic value.

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Determine the border subrank of a generic tensor and give conditions for a tensor to have border subrank higher than the generic one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ be a $d$-way tensor over the complex numbers. The subrank $Q(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle := \sum_{i=1}^r e_i^{\otimes d}$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps $A_1, \ldots, A_d : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^r$ in each tensor factor, i.e., $(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)\, T = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Euclidean (equivalently Zariski) closure of the set of tensors obtainable from $T$ in this way; equivalently, $\underline{Q}(T) \geq r$ if there exist families of linear maps $A_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}(A_1(\varepsilon) \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d(\varepsilon))\,T = \langle r \rangle$.

(a) Determine the exact value of the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ for a generic tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$, as a function of $n$ and $d$.

(b) Give explicit (algebraic or geometric) conditions on a tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ that characterize when $\underline{Q}(T)$ is strictly greater than this generic value.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024) established that the generic border subrank of a tensor in $(\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ has growth rate $\Theta(n^{1/(d-1))})$, matching the generic subrank asymptotically, via a generalized Hilbert–Mumford criterion. However, an exact closed-form value for the generic border subrank for all $n, d$ and explicit conditions characterizing tensors of strictly higher border subrank are not yet fully established, so the problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Border subrank via a generalised Hilbert-Mumford criterion
status_evidence.snippet: The border subrank of a sufficiently general tensor in (C^n)^{\otimes d} is O(n^{1/(d-1)}) for n → ∞, matching the generic subrank growth rate.
status_evidence.claim: Generic border subrank has growth rate Θ(n^{1/(d-1)}), but no exact closed-form determined.

status_evidence.title: Generic Border Subrank (workshop, March 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Workshop dedicated to the topic of generic border subrank indicates ongoing active research.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains an active research focus.
